quests.instruction: You read every instruction carefully before starting the science experiment. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Slowing down to check details before starting something new feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Slowing down to check details before starting something new gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: Scientists always read instructions carefully first — it is one of the keys to a safe, successful experiment!

quests.instruction: You throw both hands in the air the second your team is announced as finalists. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Bursting into celebration the moment you hear great news feels bright and eager.
quests.explanation: Bursting into celebration the moment you hear great news gives you a bright, eager feeling.
quests.funFact: Big, bursting celebrations like this are a fun way teams share their excitement together!

quests.instruction: You promised to practice piano but played video games instead. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Not following through on a promise to yourself can weigh on your mind.
quests.explanation: Not following through on a promise to yourself can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Starting fresh tomorrow is always an option — one missed practice does not undo all the others!

quests.instruction: You wonder if your handwriting looks messy next to your classmates'. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Comparing a skill you are still learning to others can make you doubt yourself.
quests.explanation: Comparing a skill you are still learning to others can give you a small, self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Handwriting is a skill that keeps improving with practice, no matter where you start!

quests.instruction: The amusement park is so big and busy that you do not know where to start. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Having far too many exciting choices all at once can make your mind feel jumbled.
quests.explanation: Having far too many exciting choices all at once can give your mind a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Picking just one ride to start with can help a big, busy place feel much more manageable!

quests.instruction: You ask an adult to check the water temperature before you get in the bath. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Asking for help to check something before using it feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Asking for help to check something before using it gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: Checking water temperature is a smart safety habit for kids and grown-ups alike!

quests.instruction: You beg to join every single activity at the school fair. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wanting to try absolutely everything because you are so excited feels bright and eager.
quests.explanation: Wanting to try absolutely everything because you are so excited gives you a bright, eager feeling.
quests.funFact: This bursting eagerness to try everything is a wonderful sign of curiosity and joy!

quests.instruction: You forgot your promise to help your mom with the dishes. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Realizing you broke a promise you made can weigh on your mind.
quests.explanation: Realizing you broke a promise you made can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Following through the very next time is a great way to show you still keep your word.

quests.instruction: You are the only one who has not lost a tooth yet in your class. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Noticing you are different from everyone else in a small way can make you doubt yourself.
quests.explanation: Noticing you are different from everyone else in a small way can give you a self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Losing baby teeth happens on a different schedule for every single person — there is no rush!

quests.instruction: You have five different friends asking you five different questions at the same time. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Too many questions coming at you all at once can make your mind feel full and jumbled.
quests.explanation: Too many questions coming at you all at once can give your mind a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking friends to take turns is a simple way to help this jumbled feeling settle down.

quests.instruction: You hold the railing tightly while walking down the steep stairs. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Taking extra care on something that could be risky feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Taking extra care on something that could be risky gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: Holding a railing on steep stairs is a simple habit that helps prevent slips and falls!

quests.instruction: You tell everyone you meet about the new book series you just discovered. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wanting to share exciting news with everyone you meet feels bright and eager.
quests.explanation: Wanting to share exciting news with everyone you meet gives you a bright, eager feeling.
quests.funFact: Sharing a favorite book with others is a wonderful way to spread the joy of reading!

quests.instruction: You said something unkind to your sibling and cannot stop thinking about it. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Replaying unkind words you wish you could take back can weigh on your mind.
quests.explanation: Replaying unkind words you wish you could take back can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: A sincere apology is one of the best ways to help this heavy feeling turn into a fresh start.

quests.instruction: You wonder if your new haircut looks strange compared to before. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Worrying about how a change in how you look will be seen by others can make you doubt yourself.
quests.explanation: Worrying about how a change in your appearance will be seen by others can give you a self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Most new haircuts feel strange to us at first simply because we are not used to seeing them yet!

quests.instruction: You are trying to pack for a trip while also finishing your homework and chores. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Juggling too many tasks at the exact same time can make everything feel like too much.
quests.explanation: Juggling too many tasks at the exact same time can give you a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Doing one task fully before starting the next can help a jumbled feeling untangle quickly!

quests.instruction: You read the whole recipe before turning on the stove. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Preparing carefully before starting something that needs close attention feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Preparing carefully before starting something that needs close attention gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: Reading a whole recipe first helps cooks avoid missing an important step along the way!

quests.instruction: You cheer loudly and clap the moment your teacher announces a class trip. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Bursting into cheers the instant you hear exciting news feels bright and eager.
quests.explanation: Bursting into cheers the instant you hear exciting news gives you a bright, eager feeling.
quests.funFact: A whole class cheering together is a fun way excitement can spread from person to person!

quests.instruction: You blamed your sibling for something you actually did. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Knowing you let someone else take the blame for your own mistake can weigh on your mind.
quests.explanation: Knowing you let someone else take the blame for your own mistake can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Telling the truth, even when it is hard, is the surest way to help this heavy feeling lift.

quests.instruction: You wonder if your answer in class was silly compared to everyone else's. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Replaying something you said and doubting it afterward can feel unsettling.
quests.explanation: Replaying something you said and doubting it afterward can give you a self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Teachers say there is rarely such a thing as a silly question or a silly honest answer!

quests.instruction: You have so many chores, homework, and practice all in one evening. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Having too many responsibilities packed into one evening can make everything feel like too much.
quests.explanation: Having too many responsibilities packed into one evening can give you a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Writing everything down in order of importance can help a busy evening feel less like too much at once.

quests.instruction: You look both ways twice before crossing the quiet street. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Taking extra care to check for safety, even when it seems quiet, feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Taking extra care to check for safety, even when it seems quiet, gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: Looking twice, even on quiet streets, is one of the best safety habits you can build!

quests.instruction: You jump up cheering the moment your coach announces a new tournament. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Bursting with energy and excitement about something new coming up feels bright and eager.
quests.explanation: Bursting with energy and excitement about something new coming up gives you a bright, eager feeling.
quests.funFact: Coaches say this kind of bursting energy often helps a whole team feel more motivated together!

quests.instruction: You forgot to feed your goldfish and it seems less lively than usual. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Realizing you forgot a responsibility for someone who depends on you can weigh on your mind.
quests.explanation: Realizing you forgot a responsibility for someone who depends on you can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Setting a daily reminder is a simple way to help make sure a pet's needs are never forgotten again.

quests.instruction: You are the shortest one in your class picture and wonder if people will notice. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Noticing a physical difference from your classmates can make you doubt yourself a little.
quests.explanation: Noticing a physical difference from your classmates can give you a small, self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Kids grow at very different rates and times — height differences even out over the years!

quests.instruction: You have a huge pile of laundry, dishes, and homework all waiting at once. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Seeing several big tasks piled up together can make everything feel like too much at once.
quests.explanation: Seeing several big tasks piled up together can give you a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Tackling the smallest pile first is a simple trick that helps big jobs feel less like too much.

quests.instruction: You double-check your bike helmet straps before riding down the hill. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Checking your safety gear before doing something exciting feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Checking your safety gear before doing something exciting gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: A properly fastened helmet is one of the best ways to stay safe while riding downhill!

quests.instruction: You beg your parents to sign you up the moment you hear about the new class. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wanting to start something new right away because you are so excited feels bright and eager.
quests.explanation: Wanting to start something new right away because you are so excited gives you a bright, eager feeling.
quests.funFact: This bursting eagerness often leads kids to discover a brand-new favorite activity!

quests.instruction: You forgot your grandma's birthday call yesterday. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Realizing you missed something important to someone you love can weigh on your mind.
quests.explanation: Realizing you missed something important to someone you love can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: A warm call the very next day is a lovely way to make up for a missed one!

quests.instruction: You wonder if your idea for the group project is good enough to share. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Hesitating to share an idea because you doubt it can feel unsettling.
quests.explanation: Hesitating to share an idea because you doubt it can give you a self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Many great group projects started with an idea someone almost did not share!

quests.instruction: Everyone in the busy classroom is talking to you all at once. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Too many voices coming at you at the same time can make your mind feel full and jumbled.
quests.explanation: Too many voices coming at you at the same time can give your mind a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking one person to talk at a time can help this busy, jumbled feeling calm down quickly.
